script.base: Pick'em in a closed roof: BUF is a 1.5-point road favorite with implied totals BUF 23.0 and HOU 21.5, so the book expects a one-score game and both quarterbacks on the field all day. Pace is normal, not a 44-point shootout and not a clock-killing blowout. The favorite-runs-late bump for James Cook is real only if BUF actually leads, and a one-score lead does not script a 107-yard rushing day. HOU +1.5 is inside 3.5, so the dog-throws-more rule is weak; Woody Marks and David Montgomery should both see a normal committee share if it stays close.
script.flip1: BUF jumps up by two scores early, then runs the clock. Cook's carries spike late and the 107.5 rush under dies; HOU abandons the run so Marks (46.5) and Montgomery (32.5) rush lines die while Nico Collins, Dalton Schultz, Marvin Harrison Jr and Jayden Higgins see forced targets.
script.flip2: Shootout through the 44.5: both passing games stay hot, Shakir/Moore/Collins/Schultz/Harrison clear, and Cook's rush stalls because BUF never gets a late run script. The other way, a turnover slog drags the total under and every yardage over dies together.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the under lost because BUF led by 10-plus at half, the lead-RB carry bump the spread scan already flags showed up, and Cook added one explosive run to finish over 107.5 the way two of his last four prior-season games already reached 107 and 117. The closing line at 107.5 may have been the sharp number, the unprinted season median may already have lived there, and a week-1 featured script with Johnson limited would have piled touches on Cook rather than Davis. That counter is why this is a lean flag, not a strong bet.
slip_story: One story only: moderate 44.5, closed roof, one-score game, no blowout padding. The only leg that survives the base script and the shootout flip is Cook rush yards under 107.5. No second leg cleared the pre-mortem, so there is no 3-4 leg slip, no TD, no receptions market, and no mix of this under with same-game overs. Never place the bet.
